The issues with being branded a "hate site":
1- The website can't be accessed in several places, such as work, school, etc.
2- The website could get you in trouble at work. Concerns of "So-and-so was visiting a hate site" will probably discourage some users.
3- Right now there's a huge push to get companies to be "good citizens" and refuse service to "hate sites". Since there's only a few companies that can defend a site like this from a DDOS, that's a long term risk- if they are all shut down or sued or whatever, it may become either illegal or effectively impossible to block DDOS. Then the botnets will just keep the site down for months on end, most assuredly during an election.
4- Being branded a "hate site" could discourage some people who don't even have those concerns about work or school- people who would be at home among T_D folks, but not in, say /v/niggers. The fact that they wouldn't have to go talk with or even see those folks if they don't want to may not even register if the branding sticks.

Only (4) is generally of no concern to an average voater. I bring up (1), (2), and (3) as being of concern to existing voaters, T_D folks, and the intersection of folks who are both. Right now, voat is NOT listed as a "hate site". It is listed as "social media". Adding a bunch of T_D folks won't make it have any more "hate" on it than before (per capita I would assume it would have less), but it MIGHT elevate it as a valuable target to the foes of free speech.
